app.title: FLAIL! Tools
app.description: Rolls dungeons, caves, wizard towers and hexcrawl locations for FLAIL!, draws them a map, and gives you a link that rebuilds exactly what you saw.

licence.independentHtml: FLAIL! Tools is an independent production by the flail-tools contributors and is not affiliated with Games Omnivorous. It is published under the Games Omnivorous Third-Party Licence.
licence.copyrightHtml: FLAIL is copyright of Games Omnivorous.
licence.contentHtml: The Games Omnivorous Third-Party Licence permits reusing FLAIL!'s rules, mechanics, terminology and random tables, table entries included, and still forbids reproducing its artwork or its written prose. The five generator tables here are the book's own, reproduced in face order. Its prose and its artwork are not, and this is no substitute for the rules: it builds the bones of a site and leaves every judgement the procedures ask for to you. Games Omnivorous publish the rulebook free and sell it as a physical boxset. You will want it.

messages.landingLede: Tools for running FLAIL! at the table. Free, in the browser, with no account to make and nothing kept anywhere.
messages.landingSiteBody: Roll a dungeon, a cave, a wizard tower or a hexcrawl location, each one drawn its own map. Lock the parts you like and roll the rest again; the link rebuilds exactly what you were looking at, locks and all.
messages.landingDiceBody: Roll where the whole party can see it — To Hit pools, saves at or under an attribute, and anything else in ordinary notation. The dice go straight between browsers, so nobody is hosting it: close the tab and the table is gone.
messages.landingAboutBody: where the tables come from, how the dice reach the other players, and the licence all of this is published under.
messages.mapAlt: A hand-drawn map of the site
messages.noContentBody: The generator, the maps and the seeds are all working, but the tables came back with no rows in them, so every field is blank. This normally means the data files did not load rather than that anything was rolled badly.
messages.diceTagline: Roll where the whole party can see it.
messages.diceNameNeeded: Put a name in first, so the rest of the table knows whose dice those were.
messages.diceNotationBad: That is not a roll this understands. Try d20, 2d6+1, or 4d6kh3 to keep the best three of four.
messages.diceTableBad: That is not a table code.
messages.diceStatusAway: Not at a table — these rolls are only on this screen.
messages.diceStatusFailed: This browser would not open a connection. Rolls still work here; they just stay here.
messages.hit/fumble: A fumble — hit an ally for d8, or mark usage on a carried item.
messages.hit/minor: Minor Hit — weapon damage, less defence.
messages.hit/major: Major Hit — double weapon damage, less defence.
messages.hit/death: Death Blow — the target is eliminated.
messages.diceInviteHint: Anyone with this link joins the table. Anyone with this code can listen to it, so share it the way you would share a door key.
messages.dicePrivacyHint: Rolls travel straight between browsers, encrypted, with no server in the middle and nothing stored anywhere. Close the tab and the table is gone.
messages.diceSecretHint: A private roll tells the table that you rolled and nothing else. The dice never leave this browser.
messages.dicePokerHint: A To Hit roll also reports its poker results, because that is what talents, legendary weapons and most of the bestiary trigger on — a Cutthroat rolling two pairs strikes again. What the trigger does is on your sheet; this only tells you it fired.
messages.diceEdgeHint: Advantage is one more d6 on a To Hit, or a second d20 with the kinder result kept on a save. They stack to three dice and cancel each other out.
messages.diceNatHint: Some networks will not let two browsers talk directly, and there is no relay to fall back on. If somebody never appears, paste them the seed beside a roll — it rebuilds the same dice anywhere.
